items.title: Bela Fleck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 7, 2004
items.q: Victor wants this time to do something. I’ve got a call to do this. Jeff might have this. Future Man might have this. But we have to work enough to keep this great crew that we have.

ctx.x: As a leader of a group, do you ever have to make difficult decisions that make your bandmates unhappy?

Once in a while, although everybody is really good. They really understand because they all lead themselves. They all have their own groups and situations that they have to make those kinds of decisions about and I think that they are pretty cool with most things. Usually everything is about accommodation. That’s what the challenges are. Victor wants this time to do something. I’ve got a call to do this. Jeff might have this. Future Man might have this. But we have to work enough to keep this great crew that we…

everybody in the group could get to do cool stuff outside the group but me, who had all these great opportunities I was turning down all the time. But I never talked to them about it. It was just something that was going on in my own head and gradually I realized that I had to take care of myself too, that I had to be part of the equation of making everybody happy.
